dedupe_keys.name: energy and ai future grid and water stress due to data centers pnnl presentation 2025

description: This DOE Data Explorer entry is a presentation evaluating future grid and water stress due to data centres built for artificial intelligence. Contents: an abstract noting that recent projections indicate up to 15 percent annual growth in data centre electricity demand within 5 to 10 years, that utilities' reserve margins are roughly that size so new loads could threaten resource adequacy unless data centres bring their own generation, negotiate interruptible loads or new capacity and transmission are built, and that cooling technology and location could threaten water adequacy in water-scarce regions. Authors are Kendall Mongird, Casey Burleyson, Kerem Ziya Akdemir, Travis Thurber and Jennie Rice; published 2025-06-15 with DOI 10.57931/2572012. Producer: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, sponsored by the USDOE Office of Science. Coverage: the United States. Access: public OSTI record and document download. Licence and cost: free; no reuse licence is stated. Caveats: the projections are described as large but highly uncertain, and only the presentation, not underlying data files, is provided. Simulation uses: the scenarios frame data centre load growth and water demand for grid resource-adequacy and water-stress analyses. Related record: IM3 demand projections with data centre load (data-im3-epri-datacenter-load-projections).
